title: Curie architecture atlas
subtitle: The production loop, its swappable seams, and the distance between current state and vision.

architectureGroups.label: Channel surface
architectureGroups.subtitle: 1 current · 2 planned
architectureGroups.description: One stable channel role in the architecture. Concrete surfaces are implementations of this role and stay inside this expandable node.

architectureGroups.label: Sandbox substrate
architectureGroups.subtitle: 2 proven implementations
architectureGroups.description: The stable substrate role beneath sandbox lifecycle. Kubernetes and Docker prove that the same boundary has multiple implementations.

overview.title: The request-to-reply loop
overview.description: Read left to right. Every colored connector is a seam: green is proven, yellow is clean but unproven, red is intertwined, and blue is planned.

stages.label: External surfaces
stages.description: A person, repository, or operator starts work.

stages.label: Ingress + API
stages.description: Authenticate, bind the agent, and turn the event into work.

stages.label: Queue + worker
stages.description: Claim delivery, lock the conversation, and resolve the run.

stages.label: Sandbox + runner
stages.description: Start or resume an isolated, steerable ACI session.

stages.label: Harness + MCP + model
stages.description: Run the multi-turn model loop, call hosted MCP tools, and produce side effects.

return.label: stream result, request approval when needed, then reply to the originating surface

rails.label: Approval loop
rails.description: Pause, authorize, and resume a live turn.

rails.label: Evidence plane
rails.description: Traces, telemetry, eval cases, scores, and results surround every run.

rails.label: Substrate
rails.description: Kubernetes is the production baseline; Docker proves the same sandbox boundary locally.

maturityRubric.label: Proven
maturityRubric.definition: Multiple real implementations have exercised the same boundary.

maturityRubric.label: Clean, unproven
maturityRubric.definition: One real implementation sits behind a credible boundary, but a second implementation has not tested the shape.

maturityRubric.label: Intertwined
maturityRubric.definition: A swap still requires coordinated knowledge or changes across implementation owners.

maturityRubric.label: Planned / reserved
maturityRubric.definition: The intended line is documented, but there is not a real implementation to score.

sources.title: Swappable jobs around an opinionated core

nodes.label: Slack
nodes.subtitle: Surface today
nodes.description: The only registered production channel kind today. Bolt Socket Mode handles ingress; Slack Web API renders replies and approval cards.

nodes.label: Email
nodes.subtitle: Next surface
nodes.description: Named in the product vision as a next channel. No first-party adapter is shipped on the current release.

nodes.label: Teams
nodes.subtitle: Future surface
nodes.description: Named in the vision, but deliberately deferred until a real second channel teaches the adapter interface.

nodes.label: Curie CLI
nodes.subtitle: Agent-facing control
nodes.description: Drives skill, local, and cluster loops. The local/cluster message verbs can replace Slack ingress and reply transport without changing the worker path.

nodes.label: GitHub
nodes.subtitle: Push / PR trigger
nodes.description: Webhook and outbound commit polling converge on the API git-flow engine. Dev pushes build and evaluate; production pushes promote.

nodes.label: External hook
nodes.subtitle: HMAC-triggered turn
nodes.description: A named, HMAC-authenticated API hook creates a bounded webhook-sourced turn. Bundle-declared hook lifecycle and schedules remain planned.

nodes.label: Console UI
nodes.subtitle: Operations surface
nodes.description: A real API-backed console for fleet, runs, metrics, cost, logs, versions, evals, approvals, and memory. Usage and Settings remain honest stubs.

nodes.label: Dispatcher
nodes.subtitle: Ingress · dedupe · placeholder
nodes.description: Normalizes Slack events and Block Kit text into QueuedTurn, records every adapter-owned refusal through an enumerated drop contract, claims event ids for deduplication, posts the placeholder, and appends to the run stream.

nodes.label: Port adapter service
nodes.subtitle: Third-party channel edge
nodes.description: The accepted placement for a concrete email, Teams, or third-party adapter: a deployed service, not a bundle-loaded plugin. Generic HTTP ingress and egress already ship, but no supported adapter service, install flow, or conformance kit exists.

nodes.label: Channel HTTP edge
nodes.subtitle: Generic ingress + egress
nodes.description: The API mints row-scoped channel tokens and platform-owned QueuedTurn records; ReplySinkRouter can send neutral reply events through HttpReplyAdapter. This is shipped infrastructure, not a finished email adapter.

nodes.label: API
nodes.subtitle: Control plane · git flow
nodes.description: Owns agents, versions, deployments, channel bindings, approvals, state, connector rendering, bundle validation, git-flow deploys, and read proxies.

nodes.label: Valkey streams
nodes.subtitle: Runs · evals · delivery
nodes.description: At-least-once streams carry run and eval jobs. Shared consumer machinery provides bounded delivery and dead-letter handling.

nodes.label: Worker kernel
nodes.subtitle: Route · claim · steer · recover
nodes.description: The concurrency hub: resolves the active deployment, enforces one live session per conversation, selects steer versus fresh turn, protects side effects, and reclaims crashed delivery only after sustained renewable-lease absence with one recovery owner.

nodes.label: Approval plane
nodes.subtitle: Durable human gate
nodes.description: A gate terminates the turn as AWAITING_APPROVAL, persists a durable record, suspends the sandbox, and later resumes through a new queued resolution turn.

nodes.label: Eval plane
nodes.subtitle: Cases · graders · report
nodes.description: The same bundle-carried eval suite runs across skill, local, local-release, and cluster. Worker scores and records cases, then reports a rollup to the API.

nodes.label: Sandbox
nodes.subtitle: One isolated session
nodes.description: An isolated runtime claimed per conversation. Kubernetes Agent Sandbox is production; Docker runs the same image locally.

nodes.label: Runner / ACI server
nodes.subtitle: Multi-turn session loop
nodes.description: Serves event, steer, interrupt, and reset; translates harness events into the frozen NDJSON union; injects memory and history; emits telemetry.

nodes.label: Claude harness
nodes.subtitle: Declared package today
nodes.description: The only production harness contribution. ModelSession exists, but raw SDK messages and the Claude Code plugin format still cross the conceptual boundary.

nodes.label: Model endpoint
nodes.subtitle: Provider-selected inference
nodes.description: Anthropic is the default; OpenRouter, Zhipu, Moonshot, DeepSeek, and opt-in Ollama routes are also built. Native OpenAI wire format remains absent.

nodes.label: MCP connector hosts
nodes.subtitle: Collapsed MCP implementations
nodes.description: The stable MCP role in the architecture. Bundle-declared local and remote MCP servers stay collapsed behind this host boundary, so adding another server does not add another architecture box.

nodes.label: MCP OAuth gateway
nodes.subtitle: Per-person delegated access
nodes.description: The accepted vision boundary for delegated MCP authorization. The control plane owns OAuth discovery, PKCE, encrypted tokens, refresh, revocation, and grants; the gateway applies the active run principal's grant without exposing raw OAuth tokens to the runner.

nodes.label: Agent Proxy
nodes.subtitle: Credentials + egress boundary
nodes.description: Draft architecture moves provider credentials and enforceable egress policy out of the sandbox. It is a decision candidate, not shipped architecture.

nodes.label: OTel collector
nodes.subtitle: Telemetry write port
nodes.description: Receives OTLP from the runner and exports to Langfuse over HTTP. The write boundary is mostly vendor-neutral.

nodes.label: Langfuse
nodes.subtitle: Traces · metrics · eval scores
nodes.description: The current trace and eval store. The API reconstructs trees and metrics through a vendor-specific read adapter; ClickHouse backs the deployment.

nodes.label: Postgres
nodes.subtitle: Control-plane state
nodes.description: Stores agents, versions, deployments, channel bindings, approvals, memory, history, and other durable control-plane state.

nodes.label: RustFS / S3
nodes.subtitle: Immutable bundles
nodes.description: Stores immutable agent bundles and eval inputs behind an S3-compatible protocol and ObjectStore port.

nodes.label: Kubernetes
nodes.subtitle: Production substrate
nodes.description: Baseline production substrate: platform services, Agent Sandbox CRDs, security rails, connector workloads, and observability dependencies.

nodes.label: Docker
nodes.subtitle: Local parity substrate
nodes.description: Runs the same worker and runner image locally behind the same SandboxClient contract.

seams.label: Channel ingress + binding
seams.contract: QueuedTurn + ReplyHandle; neutral {kind, address} deployment binding
seams.reason: The core payload, binding, and per-turn endpoint are channel-neutral, but only Slack is registered as a production kind.
seams.leakage: TurnSource.SLACK still names the human-authored channel case generically, and one production adapter does not prove two coexisting channel implementations.
seams.nextStep: Ship one real second channel through the existing wire before designing a general registry.

seams.label: Reply delivery semantics
seams.implementations: 1 production channel plus SlackReplyAdapter and generic HttpReplyAdapter
seams.contract: ReplySink.emit over turn.status, reply.update, reply.post, and turn.completed
seams.reason: ReplySink, ReplySinkRouter, four versioned events, and generic HTTP egress are shipped, but no second production channel has proven their semantics.
seams.leakage: A second channel without edit-in-place must define how streamed updates, platform-owned posts, acknowledgements, and settled approval state map to its surface.
seams.nextStep: Implement email (or another real channel) and let its delivery constraints finalize post/update/stream policy.

seams.label: Semantic channel interaction
seams.implementations: 2 real renderers (Slack Block Kit, terminal selector)
seams.contract: Versioned OutboundMessage with text fallback, Choice, Confirm, and semantic action values
seams.reason: Two distinct surfaces render the same semantic message without putting their widgets in the contract.
seams.leakage: The terminal mirror is handwritten and capabilities are modeled but not dynamically negotiated.
seams.nextStep: Generate or drift-gate the Rust mirror; wire capability negotiation when a second production channel needs it.

seams.label: Queue / stream broker
seams.implementations: 1 real broker (Valkey) behind producer and consumer ports
seams.contract: StreamPublisher + StreamBroker ports, frozen payload field, and shared bounded consumer
seams.reason: The port and consumer invariants are explicit, but a second broker has not exercised them.
seams.leakage: Some API producers and graveyard readers still bypass the ports; the adjacent consumer-liveness store, set verbs, and redis-py exception types also leak Valkey semantics.
seams.nextStep: No speculative adapter; promote only if a real broker demand appears.

seams.label: Sandbox substrate
seams.contract: Six-method SandboxClient claim lifecycle plus ClaimView and SandboxView outcome types
seams.reason: The same kernel and runner operate through two materially different runtime implementations.
seams.leakage: SandboxView.port, model-credential forwarding, connector-secret delivery, warm-pool behavior, and production capacity still differ across Kubernetes and Docker.
seams.nextStep: Keep parity tests focused on the shared outcomes; do not turn substrate choice into a product axis.

seams.label: Frozen ACI protocol
seams.contract: SessionConfig, boot env, HTTP control verbs, and versioned NDJSON events across Python/TS/Rust
seams.reason: This is the strongest documented boundary, but only one production harness stack has proven it end to end.
seams.leakage: A non-Claude harness must still consume or translate the Claude Code plugin bundle shape.
seams.nextStep: Use the conformance guide against a genuinely different production harness.

seams.label: Runner ↔ harness / ModelSession
seams.contract: In-process ModelSession protocol and declared harness contribution
seams.reason: The named protocol is real, but its message union is still SDK-shaped and the bundle distribution format is Claude Code verbatim.
seams.leakage: A foreign harness must emit Claude SDK-shaped objects or replace the runner adapter while also interpreting the Claude plugin format.
seams.nextStep: Prove the out-of-process ACI boundary with a second harness; keep provider-native checkpointing an optional capability.

seams.label: Declared harness package
seams.contract: HarnessContribution manifest; built-ins resolve directly and third-party contributions use curie.harness entry points
seams.reason: Selection and declared assets are clean, but there is no second real package and third-party conformance remains unproven.
seams.leakage: The registry currently wraps the same built-in adapter rather than demonstrating substitution.
seams.nextStep: Publish and run contribution conformance against a non-built-in package.

seams.label: Model provider + credentials
seams.implementations: Multiple live endpoints through one Claude-SDK / Anthropic-wire strategy
seams.contract: Declared wire protocol, provider endpoint, canonical credential keys, and boot-env forwarding
seams.reason: Several endpoints exercise routing and credential resolution, but they do not represent multiple independent provider or harness implementations of the boundary.
seams.leakage: Native OpenAI wire format is absent; several providers share compatibility routing rather than independent harness implementations.
seams.nextStep: Add native OpenAI wire only when its semantics are tested through the live-provider parity tier.

seams.label: Telemetry / OTLP
seams.implementations: 1 trace backend (Langfuse) behind an OTel collector
seams.contract: OTLP write path + Curie API DTO read path
seams.reason: The write protocol is standard and the UI sees Curie DTOs, but only Langfuse has exercised both sides.
seams.leakage: Vendor attributes and /langfuse URL namespaces leak into the otherwise neutral boundary; the read adapter spans multiple modules.
seams.nextStep: Map vendor span attributes in the collector and neutralize read-route naming.

seams.label: Eval case + scorer
seams.implementations: Multiple grader kinds plus a trajectory matcher across Python and Rust
seams.contract: Frozen eval-case schema + shared trajectory vectors + tri-state outcomes
seams.reason: Distinct scoring implementations and two languages exercise the case boundary, with shared fixtures pinning semantics.
seams.leakage: Python and Rust still implement graders separately; cluster answer-quality failure is not yet universally fatal.
seams.nextStep: Land semantic provenance verification before making cluster answer-quality promotion fatal.

seams.label: Eval result store
seams.contract: Eval recorder write + EvalMatrix read DTO + version:/suite: tag convention
seams.reason: The platform owns the result shape, but only one backend and one unfrozen tag convention have exercised it.
seams.leakage: The recorder and matrix reader encode Langfuse tags and API behavior directly.
seams.nextStep: Record or freeze the tag convention; wait for a real second store before inventing a generic adapter.

seams.label: Blob storage
seams.contract: ObjectStore port + shared S3 client + bundle-fetch init path
seams.reason: The port is explicit and S3-compatible services are configuration swaps, but no non-S3 implementation has tested the abstraction.
seams.leakage: API and worker use separate async/sync adapters, while bucket bootstrap, init containers, migration, and key-free auth retain S3-specific obligations.
seams.nextStep: Leave it alone until a real non-S3 demand appears.

seams.label: Relational database
seams.contract: SQLAlchemy models + Alembic migrations + DSN
seams.reason: Managed Postgres is a clean operational swap, but another SQL engine has not exercised the model boundary.
seams.leakage: Postgres UUID, JSONB, schema qualification, native enums, DISTINCT ON SQL, and asyncpg-specific JSONB decoding remain in application code.
seams.nextStep: Keep Postgres opinionated unless a concrete alternate engine demand emerges.

seams.label: Approval authorizer
seams.implementations: 3 real approver sets (channel, user group, explicit users)
seams.contract: ApproverSet / ApprovalCreator + durable semantic approval record
seams.reason: Three distinct membership strategies exercise one API-owned authorization interface.
seams.leakage: Authenticated principal semantics and the single-operator dead end remain active draft decisions.
seams.nextStep: Land structured authenticated principals before extending approval authority to new channels.

seams.label: Approval principal identity
seams.implementations: Caller-asserted operator identity plus channel-specific actor facts
seams.contract: No single authenticated principal contract across chat, console, and operator resolution
seams.reason: The authorizer resolves membership cleanly, but the identity presented to resolution is not yet one structured, authenticated principal across entry points.
seams.leakage: Caller-asserted resolved_by and actor_channel semantics cross API keys, Slack facts, console sessions, and operator commands.
seams.nextStep: Land ADR-0106's canonical principals and negative identity proofs before broadening multi-channel approval authority.

seams.label: Workflow state store
seams.implementations: 1 state API router over Postgres JSONB
seams.contract: Scoped namespace/key document API with size limits and CAS behavior
seams.reason: The HTTP state router is useful, but not every state consumer stays behind it; operator memory and relational paths can bypass the supposed boundary.
seams.leakage: A second state backend would not cover direct model/JSONB access, while memory and transcript loaders still depend on the HTTP shape and capacity limits.
seams.nextStep: Inventory and close bypasses before extracting another backend; then treat retention, capacity, and back-pressure as one admission policy.

seams.label: Agent memory
seams.contract: MemoryStore load/append, optional replace, and boot-preamble injection over a scoped state token
seams.reason: The loader port and null implementation are clean, but no alternate durable memory backend has exercised them.
seams.leakage: The operator inspect/seed/edit/delete plane addresses the Postgres WorkflowStateEntry backing directly instead of going through MemoryStore.
seams.nextStep: Keep the operator plane and any future loader consistent before adding another backing; automatic learned-record extraction remains future work.

seams.label: Conversation history
seams.contract: TranscriptStore load/append + deterministic per-agent/thread reference
seams.reason: The harness-neutral replay path is explicit, but only one store and prompt-preamble rehydration have proven it.
seams.leakage: Stored append logs remain unbounded under state-store caps; replay is semantic, not token-exact or native-session restoration.
seams.nextStep: Keep portable replay mandatory; add native checkpoints only as an optional harness capability.

seams.label: Trigger ingestion
seams.implementations: 4 hardcoded trigger paths (Slack, GitHub webhook, commit poller, generic HMAC hook)
seams.contract: No unified runtime trigger port; API hooks mint bounded webhook-sourced turns while bundle declarations and schedules remain planned
seams.reason: Several triggers exist, but they do not implement one shared trigger interface or one event lifecycle.
seams.leakage: Slack enters through dispatcher while GitHub, polling, and generic hooks enter through API-specific handlers; bundle-declared hooks and schedules are not consumed.
seams.nextStep: Connect declarations and schedules to the shipped bounded hook lifecycle before expanding trigger types.

seams.label: Agent-facing CLI output
seams.implementations: 40 typed outputs behind one trait across many verbs
seams.contract: CliOutput + Ui.emit + versioned JSON result schemas
seams.reason: Many independent command results exercise the same human/JSON emission boundary.
seams.leakage: A tracked set of legacy/operator verbs still has inline or unstructured success output.
seams.nextStep: Finish migrating the tracked exceptions without widening the output contract.

seams.label: MCP connector host
seams.contract: Bundle declaration → rendered connector workload → MCP reachability
seams.reason: The typed client exposes raw Kubernetes JSON, rendering is Kubernetes-specific outside the port, and CLI and reconciler paths do not share identical apply/prune semantics.
seams.leakage: Build inputs, pinned images, delegated OAuth, runtime injection, reconciliation, and Kubernetes objects cross control-plane and cluster ownership.
seams.nextStep: Close runtime injection and converge CLI/reconciler lifecycle before calling the host portable.

seams.label: MCP service-key authentication
seams.contract: Named connector secret → platform-hosted MCP environment or authorization header
seams.reason: Service credentials already cross a named secret boundary and stay owned by the deployment, but no second production identity mode has proved the abstraction.
seams.leakage: Secret rendering and delivery still span bundle declaration, API, Kubernetes, and the incomplete sealed-credential consumer path.
seams.nextStep: Keep service authentication explicit and fail closed; prove delegated OAuth as a separate identity mode with no fallback between them.

seams.label: Per-person MCP OAuth
seams.contract: Canonical run principal → principal-scoped grant → control-plane-owned OAuth gateway → MCP server
seams.reason: ADR-0088 defines the ownership and fail-closed behavior, but the gateway, grant lifecycle, connection action, and resume path are not shipped.
seams.leakage: Until implemented, MCP calls cannot safely act with each human's authority; the existing deployment service identity is the only current mode.
seams.nextStep: Implement discovery, PKCE, encrypted grant storage, refresh and revocation, then prove missing-auth pause and post-callback resume without giving the runner a raw token.

seams.label: Sealed connector credential
seams.contract: Frozen sealed-credential envelope with cluster-side opening
seams.reason: The Rust sealer and Python opener interoperate, but the product path is disconnected: validation and delivery do not yet form one working production consumer path.
seams.leakage: Security depends on exact agreement between CLI, API rendering, cluster delivery, and the currently uncalled opener.
seams.nextStep: Connect and prove the complete sealed-secret path before expanding its wire or consumers.

seams.label: Bundle / plugin format
seams.contract: Frozen Pydantic models + regenerated committed JSON Schema (no generated Rust/TS) + immutable content-addressed bundle
seams.reason: The format is strongly enforced but intentionally has one implementation and one ecosystem shape.
seams.leakage: This is the main coupling that a non-Claude harness must interpret or translate.
seams.nextStep: Do not invent another format; require alternate harnesses to demonstrate a translation strategy.

seams.label: Third-party port adapter
seams.contract: Intended deployed-service placement; no runtime implementation
seams.reason: The decision fixes ownership and placement, but there is nothing real to score.
seams.leakage: Adapter discovery, routing, credentials, conformance, and lifecycle are still future work.
seams.nextStep: Use the first real second channel as the reference adapter and promotion kit.

seams.label: Agent Proxy boundary
seams.contract: Draft credential and egress enforcement boundary outside the sandbox
seams.reason: The architecture is drafted but intentionally unimplemented.
seams.leakage: Provider credentials and web egress still enter the sandbox under current controls.
seams.nextStep: Resolve the draft's open enforcement and deployment decisions before implementation.

seams.label: Eval result → promotion authority
seams.implementations: Commit status exists; internal promotion enforcement does not
seams.contract: Reserved policy boundary between graded evidence and production deployment
seams.reason: The API reports eval state to GitHub, but process_push does not read that result before creating a production deployment.
seams.leakage: Safety depends on external branch protection and release policy rather than a product invariant.
seams.nextStep: Land semantic provenance first, then bind promotion to an authoritative graded result without rebuilding the artifact.

routes.label: state get / put / list / delete / append

flows.label: Whole system
flows.summary: Every currently visible component and route in one architecture map. Choose a specific flow to isolate and walk its path.

flows.label: Slack turn
flows.summary: A mention becomes one queued, isolated, multi-turn model session and one edited thread reply.

steps.title: Receive and deduplicate
steps.caption: Bolt receives the mention; the dispatcher claims the event id and posts the placeholder.

steps.title: Normalize ingress
steps.caption: The dispatcher serializes a channel-neutral QueuedTurn onto curie:runs.

steps.title: Claim delivery
steps.caption: The worker consumer group claims the event and acquires the conversation lock.

steps.title: Resolve and isolate
steps.caption: The binding selects agent, version, and bundle; SandboxClient claims or resumes the runtime.

steps.title: Start or steer
steps.caption: The worker sends event for a fresh turn or steer for a live one.

steps.title: Rehydrate durable memory
steps.caption: At boot the runner loads the agent memory log over the scoped state token before composing the effective prompt.

steps.title: Enter the harness
steps.caption: The runner translates the ACI request into the active ModelSession.

steps.title: Run inference
steps.caption: The declared Claude harness calls the selected provider and streams its result.

steps.title: Stream outcomes
steps.caption: The runner emits text deltas, tool notes, side-effect markers, and a terminal result as NDJSON.

steps.title: Return to the surface
steps.caption: ReplySink updates the original placeholder and the worker acknowledges the stream entry.

flows.label: Approval + resume
flows.summary: A gated tool call ends the turn, persists authority, suspends the sandbox, then resumes through a new queued event.

steps.title: Gate the side effect
steps.caption: The runner terminates AWAITING_APPROVAL; the kernel converts it into durable governance work.

steps.title: Persist the decision point
steps.caption: The API stores the approval, policy, requester, and allowed approver set.

steps.title: Render a semantic confirm
steps.caption: The worker posts a channel-neutral confirm intent; Slack renders the approval card.

steps.title: Authorize the human
steps.caption: Approve or reject reaches the API, which resolves membership rather than trusting the clicked value.

steps.title: Queue a new resolution turn
steps.caption: The original event is already acknowledged; resolution enters as its own QueuedTurn.

steps.title: Reclaim the conversation
steps.caption: The worker restores the same thread affinity and suspended sandbox.

steps.title: Resume with one-shot allowance
steps.caption: The resolution turn tells the runner whether to continue or terminate the rejected action.

steps.title: Settle the surface
steps.caption: The card becomes non-interactive and the final reply returns to the same conversation.

flows.label: PR / git deploy
flows.summary: A development branch push becomes an immutable bundle, deployment, and eval fan-out; a production push promotes the stored artifact without cloning or rebuilding it.

steps.title: Ingest a push
steps.caption: HMAC webhook or outbound commit poller converges on the same process_push function.

steps.title: Archive, validate, store
steps.caption: The API archives the SHA, validates the frozen plugin shape, and writes an immutable bundle.

steps.title: Create version + deployment
steps.caption: Dev branches activate the new version; production branches promote an existing artifact.

steps.title: Fan out evals
steps.caption: A newly built development bundle appends one deduplicated EvalJob to curie:evals.

steps.title: Grade the exact bundle
steps.caption: The eval consumer loads cases from the immutable bundle and drives the runner.

steps.title: Record evidence
steps.caption: Each case writes a trace and eval score tagged by version and suite.

steps.title: Report the rollup
steps.caption: The worker posts the result to the API.

steps.title: Publish, but do not internally gate
steps.caption: GitHub receives a commit status; production promotion still relies on external policy rather than an API invariant.

flows.label: Eval + parity ladder
flows.summary: One bundle and one case file cross skill, local, local-release, and cluster to expose environment drift.

steps.title: Pin the artifact
steps.caption: Bundle identity fixes the code, tools, and eval cases under test.

steps.title: Load the suite
steps.caption: The worker reads evals/cases.json from that exact immutable bundle.

steps.title: Choose the required tier
steps.caption: Skill, Docker, released Compose, or Kubernetes changes only the substrate rung.

steps.title: Run a fresh case
steps.caption: Each case defaults to a fresh conversation and uses the same ACI loop.

steps.title: Score the outcome
steps.caption: Text graders and trajectory matching produce pass, fail, or plumbing-only.

steps.title: Persist the evidence
steps.caption: Traces and scores support the matrix and later diagnosis.

flows.label: Observability read/write
flows.summary: The runner emits standard telemetry downward; the API turns vendor reads back into Curie DTOs for agents and humans.

steps.title: Emit the run
steps.caption: The runner writes agent, generation, tool, session, and sandbox attributes over OTLP.

steps.title: Export once
steps.caption: The collector handles Langfuse authentication and HTTP-only OTLP ingest.

steps.title: Reconstruct the evidence
steps.caption: The API reads traces, builds the tool tree, and proxies metrics and cost.

steps.title: Expose one read surface
steps.caption: Console and CLI use Curie API shapes instead of talking to Langfuse directly.

flows.label: MCP with service key
flows.summary: Today an MCP connector acts as a deployment-owned bot or service account: the platform binds its named secret and the runner talks through the collapsed MCP host boundary.

steps.title: Reconcile the hosted workload
steps.caption: The worker uses ConnectorClient to list, apply, and delete the Kubernetes connector resources derived from the bundle.

steps.title: Bind the service identity
steps.caption: The bundle names the connector secret; deployment configuration supplies the value and the platform injects it into the hosted MCP connector.

steps.title: Call the MCP server
steps.caption: The runner exchanges MCP requests and results with the hosted connector. Every human currently shares the deployment's service authority.

flows.label: Future per-person MCP OAuth
flows.summary: The accepted vision binds each run's canonical human principal to that person's OAuth grant. Curie applies the grant at a gateway, and the runner never receives the raw token.

steps.title: Resolve principal and grant
steps.caption: The control plane owns OAuth discovery, PKCE, encrypted token storage, refresh, revocation, and the principal-to-grant binding.

steps.title: Call as the run principal
steps.caption: The runner sends a principal-bound MCP request to the gateway without receiving a provider token.

steps.title: Apply delegated authority
steps.caption: The gateway applies only that principal's active grant and exchanges MCP traffic with the declared server. Missing auth pauses the run for a connection action, then resumes after callback.

flows.label: Future email channel
flows.summary: The first real second channel should prove the neutral contracts and reveal which Slack reply assumptions must change.

steps.title: Normalize email
steps.caption: A deployed adapter owns provider auth, event normalization, identities, and an opaque reply target.

steps.title: Use the shipped HTTP edge
steps.caption: The deployed adapter authenticates with a row-scoped token and posts provider-neutral input.

steps.title: Enter the same core
steps.caption: The API, not the adapter, mints the same QueuedTurn used by Slack and the CLI stub.

steps.title: Reuse the worker invariants
steps.caption: Routing, concurrency, sandboxing, approval, and recovery remain unchanged.

steps.title: Reuse the ACI
steps.caption: The agent does not learn which channel started the turn.

steps.title: Emit neutral reply events
steps.caption: ReplySinkRouter sends status, update, post, and completion events through the generic HTTP adapter.

steps.title: Return to the owning adapter
steps.caption: The platform calls the adapter endpoint selected from server-controlled binding facts.

steps.title: Teach the real delivery policy
steps.caption: Email must decide how streaming, new posts, acknowledgements, and settled approvals map without pretending to be Slack chat.update.

flows.label: Generic webhook turn
flows.summary: A named HMAC-authenticated hook becomes a bounded webhook-sourced turn on the shared run stream.

steps.title: Authenticate the named hook
steps.caption: The API verifies the per-hook HMAC and resolves the target agent.

steps.title: Mint the platform turn
steps.caption: The API creates the typed webhook-sourced QueuedTurn with bounded delivery metadata.

steps.title: Reuse bounded delivery
steps.caption: The shared consumer claims, caps, and dead-letters the hook turn like other run traffic.

steps.title: Run through the same ACI
steps.caption: The worker drives the selected bundle without a channel adapter in the path.

flows.label: Future bundle hooks
flows.summary: Generic webhook consumption ships; bundle-declared hook installation and scheduled turns remain planned.

steps.title: Reuse API-owned ingress
steps.caption: A future declaration resolves onto the shipped named-hook endpoint rather than a new dispatcher.

steps.title: Create a typed turn
steps.caption: A new event kind would carry source, authorization, concurrency, expiry, and delivery policy.

steps.title: Reuse bounded delivery
steps.caption: The shared stream consumer must still cap attempts, dead-letter, and expose failure.

adrs.title: Kubernetes Agent Sandbox as the interactive runtime substrate
adrs.summary: Kubernetes is the production runtime substrate; Docker is the parity implementation behind SandboxClient.

adrs.title: claude-agent-sdk adapter behind a frozen ACI
adrs.summary: The outer protocol is strong; the in-runner message types and plugin format retain Claude coupling.

adrs.title: Per-agent connector auth
adrs.summary: Connector credentials are named by the bundle and supplied per deployment, giving current MCP servers one service or bot identity rather than a human principal.

adrs.title: Approval gates and human-in-the-loop
adrs.summary: A gated turn persists a durable decision and resumes later through a new event.

adrs.title: A git push is the deploy
adrs.summary: Git flow, immutable bundles, and eval fan-out are built; a red eval does not yet universally enforce promotion.

adrs.title: Swappable jobs around an opinionated core
adrs.summary: One curated default per job; a second implementation teaches the interface instead of a speculative registry.

adrs.title: Rendering-free channel interface
adrs.summary: Semantic Choice and Confirm render in Slack and terminal; capability negotiation and a second production channel remain open.

adrs.title: Memory port and first loader
adrs.summary: Scoped state-backed agent memory reaches the runner as a harness-neutral boot preamble.

adrs.title: Conversation-history port and first loader
adrs.summary: A fresh or restarted sandbox rehydrates the same thread from durable transcript state, without SDK-native resume.

adrs.title: Proactive within-episode memory agent
adrs.summary: Drafts an injected within-episode memory agent; automatic generation remains absent.

adrs.title: LLM-as-a-Verifier grader and progress signal
adrs.summary: The semantic provenance grader is an accepted slot, but no verifier grader exists in Python or Rust today.

adrs.title: The harness is a declared package
adrs.summary: Harness assets and selection are declared; only the built-in Claude contribution exists.

adrs.title: Out-of-process harness boundary
adrs.summary: Would make alternate harness adapters consumable out of process across an Omnigent-compatible wire.

adrs.title: Harness conformance has teeth
adrs.summary: A reusable conformance suite exists; third-party production contributions have not yet proved it.

adrs.title: Agent Proxy credential and egress boundary
adrs.summary: Moves credentials and enforceable egress outside the sandbox; not current architecture.

adrs.title: Inbound triggers as a new event kind
adrs.summary: API-owned, HMAC-authenticated generic hooks mint typed webhook-sourced turns; declaration installation and schedules remain future work.

adrs.title: A bundle carries its own sealed connector keys
adrs.summary: Defines the cross-language sealed-box wire and cluster-owned opening key; end-to-end production delivery is not yet fully connected.

adrs.title: Bundles declare connectors; the platform hosts them
adrs.summary: The bundle declares MCP connectors and Curie derives their hosted runtime, secrets, policy, and MCP configuration; lifecycle portability remains intertwined with Kubernetes.

adrs.title: Per-user delegated OAuth for MCP
adrs.summary: Defines principal-scoped OAuth, control-plane-owned grants, a token-hiding MCP gateway, and missing-auth pause and resume semantics. The service-key mode remains separate and cannot silently substitute.

adrs.title: Tiered memory lifecycle
adrs.summary: Defines agent and channel memory tiers, lifecycle turns, trust, and bootstrap/update obligations.

adrs.title: Port adapters are deployed services
adrs.summary: Fixes placement and ownership for third-party adapters, while the actual adapter service remains unbuilt.

adrs.title: Hooks are bundle-declared turns
adrs.summary: Drafts scheduled and webhook turns with authorization, silence, concurrency, and test-fire semantics.

adrs.title: Agents search their own surface through the channel port
adrs.summary: Proposes a spike before committing channel search verbs; intentionally not current behavior.

adrs.title: External native session checkpoints
adrs.summary: Makes provider-native checkpoints an optional harness capability while retaining portable projection.

adrs.title: An approver is an authenticated principal
adrs.summary: Replaces caller-asserted approver strings with authenticated principals and makes single-operator dead ends loud.

adrs.title: An agent reads its own runs
adrs.summary: Proposes a first-party scoped runs MCP surface with structured attribution and fail-closed identity.

adrs.title: Deploy targets carry environment values
adrs.summary: Moves environment-specific non-secret values onto deploy targets while preserving connector declaration shape.

adrs.title: Retention, capacity, and back pressure are one policy
adrs.summary: Would admit claims against a coherent capacity policy instead of discovering overload after launch.

adrs.title: Deterministic security posture classification
adrs.summary: Computes posture from shipped layers and operator gates instead of trusting a configured label.

adrs.title: Default memory compaction algorithm
adrs.summary: Drafts opt-in, from-source compaction with validation, scope defaults, and an auditable write path.

investments.title: Prove the channel seam with one real second adapter
investments.why: This is the lowest-graded production job and the only way to turn several good contracts into demonstrated multi-surface architecture.
investments.unlock: Email or Teams, true multi-surface binding, per-channel streaming policy, adapter kit and conformance.

investments.title: Run a genuinely different harness through the ACI
investments.why: The outer contract is strong, but the current in-process path and bundle distribution wedge still hide the real replacement cost.
investments.unlock: Credible Codex/ADK/Strands support, truthful harness conformance, optional native checkpoints.

investments.title: Close the semantic eval and promotion gap
investments.why: The parity ladder is the product promise, but provenance quality and red-eval promotion still have reserved or validated-only clauses.
investments.unlock: Fatal cluster quality gates, meaningful source verification, stronger PR-to-production trust.

investments.title: Unify generic trigger and hook lifecycle
investments.why: Three trigger paths exist, but they are hardcoded lanes rather than one typed, bounded event lifecycle.
investments.unlock: Bundle-declared schedules/webhooks, explicit delivery destinations, shared concurrency and failure semantics.

investments.title: Move credentials and enforceable egress out of the sandbox
investments.why: The current service-key path and accepted delegated-OAuth design expose the same unresolved security boundary: credentials, principal binding, and enforceable egress still span several owners.
investments.unlock: Stronger tenant isolation, explicit service versus delegated identity, per-person MCP authority, centralized credential policy, and auditable outbound access.

investments.title: Neutralize the observability read side
investments.why: OTLP is already a good write port; vendor attributes, route names, and read modules are the remaining concentrated leakage.
investments.unlock: A practical second trace backend without UI or API contract churn.
